macro.summary: Week closes on a cooling-inflation, softening-consumer note. July CPI (Wed, in line) and July PPI (Thu, UNCHANGED m/m vs +0.2% est) both landed dovish, driving Thursday's record close. Friday's data turns from prices to the CONSUMER: July retail sales printed before the bell showing shoppers slowed spending from June, and UMich consumer sentiment (est 54.1, down from 55.2) is due 10:00 ET. That is the interesting tension for the tape -- disinflation is good for multiples, but a visibly decelerating consumer is the first thing that turns 'soft landing' into 'slowdown'. VIX 14.49 says the market is not pricing that risk at all.

watchlist._budget_constraint_found_1346Z: NEW and decisive, and no prior run had priced it: the liquid contract costs $938 for ONE (mid 9.375 x 100). Agentic premium-at-risk is $749 (the SPY hedge) against the $1,500 budget, leaving $751 of headroom. $938 > $751, so a single long 2026-09-18 105C DOES NOT FIT the agentic budget at all -- it is not a sizing preference issue, it is a hard budget breach. Two structurally valid ways a future run could own this thesis inside the budget, both of which need their own gate check: (1) a higher strike (e.g. the 110C) for less premium and less delta; (2) a DEBIT SPREAD, which is this desk's stated structural preference at this account size and would likely land near $400-450. TENSION TO RESOLVE BEFORE CHOOSING (2): INTC IV/RV is 0.85 -- IV is BELOW realized for a fifth straight reading -- so the short leg of a spread SELLS cheap vol, which is exactly backwards. The honest read is that the cheap-vol argument favors a long single-leg, and the budget favors a spread. That conflict is unresolved and is itself a reason to want a much better trigger before paying for either.
